slides.0.title: Bandol
slides.0.subtitle: Terraces, Mourvèdre and age-worthy reds
slides.1.title: Place and climate
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Restanque terraces
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Bandol's vineyards sit on stone-walled terraces (restanques) in amphitheatre-like slopes facing the sea, with abundant sun tempered by sea breezes
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Communes
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The area covers eight communes including Bandol, Le Castellet, La Cadière-d'Azur, Sanary-sur-Mer, Évenos, Ollioules, Saint-Cyr-sur-Mer and Le Beausset
slides.1.highlights.2.title: AOC
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Bandol became an AOC in 1941, among Provence's earliest
slides.1.content: Sun, sea breezes and terraces ripen late Mourvèdre.
slides.2.title: Varieties and rules
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Mourvèdre leads
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Red is built on Mourvèdre at a minimum of 50%, with Grenache and Cinsault; rosé also leans on Mourvèdre
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Ageing requirement
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Red must be aged in oak for at least 18 months before bottling and release
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Colour split
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Sources disagree on the red/rosé split (INAO about 75% rosé; others about two-thirds or nearly 70% red), so it is not tested
slides.2.content: Late-ripening and tannic; it opens with age.
slides.3.title: Style
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Red
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Dark colour, blackberry, spice and leather with firm tannins, closed when young; made for ageing
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Rosé
slides.3.highlights.1.content: More structured and food-friendly than lighter coastal rosés
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Pairing
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Red suits braised lamb, game and herb-driven Provençal dishes
slides.3.content: Bandol is Provence's rare age-worthy red.
